title: 1990 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: The annual incomes of \(1{,}000\) families range from \(\$8200\) to \(\$98{,}000.\) In error, the largest income was entered on the computer as \(\$980{,}000.\) The difference between the mean of the incorrect data and the mean of the actual data is

solutions.text:
Only one entry changed. The incorrect total exceeds the actual total by \(\$980{,}000 - \$98{,}000 = \$882{,}000.\)

Since this extra amount is spread over \(1000\) families, the means differ by \(\dfrac{\$882{,}000}{1000} = \$882.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A .
hints: Only one value changed, so only the total sum changes; the count stays at \(1000\)
Find how much the one wrong entry inflated the total, then divide that by \(1000\)
